meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
I know who you are, Hale. Who decided on Owen's zero, and when?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what it's based on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He drafts elsewhere and pastes it in when he's done, so all that shows is when it was pasted.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Give me the book. A seventeen-year-old getting a line of Shakespeare wrong is a bad citation, not proof of anything.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. What exactly are you proposing, Hale?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's what outlines are for. And you still haven't answered me.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing, tonight. Owen will do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. I want the date and time of the rewrite in that email too.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. Put it in the email, and make sure nobody from his class is in the room.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that no student from his class be present for the rewrite and that the date, time and these conditions be confirmed in writing. I expect that written confirmation from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school with nothing on his record, and she still wants it confirmed in writing tonight with nobody from his class in the room; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached well before her call.
What moved her: showing the version history with its exact times and then answering her pasting defence by asking for a dated draft, because it was specific, checkable and tied to his own work.
What cost ground: nothing lost a position, though bringing out the outline instead of answering her question about what you were proposing made her repeat herself.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she said students change their argument between outline and essay, answer that point directly before moving on, so every piece you showed is left standing.
